claims.claim: The framing joke is that Gyldayn's manuscript came handwritten on vellum with a quill and Martin merely transcribed it.
claims.source: George R.R. Martin, Not a Blog, 25 Apr 2018
claims.quote: handwritten on vellum with a quill pen

claims.claim: The Jaehaerys excerpt dates its action to a regnal year (58 AC) and advances by chronology rather than by scene.
claims.source: George R.R. Martin, Not a Blog excerpt post, 27 Sep 2018
claims.page: A FIRE & BLOOD Excerpt just for YOU!

claims.claim: Speech in the chronicle is mediated through testimony hedges such as 'is reported to have said' and 'would later tell the king'.
claims.source: George R.R. Martin, Not a Blog excerpt post, 27 Sep 2018
claims.page: A FIRE & BLOOD Excerpt just for YOU!

claims.claim: Consistent formal designations (His Grace, the queen, Lord Stark) and archaic diction sustain a courtly register with occasional colloquial flourishes.
claims.source: George R.R. Martin, Not a Blog excerpt post, 27 Sep 2018
claims.page: A FIRE & BLOOD Excerpt just for YOU!

claims.claim: Even the chronicle register carries substantial direct speech embedded in the narrative and compresses a family's history into a single sentence.
claims.source: George R.R. Martin, Not a Blog excerpt post, 27 Sep 2018
claims.page: A FIRE & BLOOD Excerpt just for YOU!

claims.claim: Martin says he loves reading popular histories and that is what he was aiming for.
claims.source: George R.R. Martin, georgerrmartin.com Fire & Blood page
claims.quote: that's what I was aiming for here
claims.page: Fire and Blood | George R.R. Martin

claims.claim: Because Gyldayn 'writes' the book, Martin says it makes sense he would not have all the information, and its mysteries are possible answers, not definitive ones.
claims.source: Winter Is Coming digest of Martin's Not a Blog comments, 3 May 2018
claims.quote: he wouldn't have all the information
claims.page: George R.R. Martin clears up misconceptions about Fire & Blood

claims.claim: The Gyldayn document opens with a long early-modern-style descriptive title ('Being A History of the Causes, Origins, Battles, and Betrayals...') plus a transcription credit.
claims.source: George R.R. Martin, 'The Princess and the Queen' excerpt (primary text), Reactor/Tor.com
claims.quote: Being A History of the Causes
claims.page: Dangerous Women: The Princess and The Queen (Excerpt)

claims.claim: The first paragraph is the historian objecting to the received name of the war and deferring to tradition anyway.
claims.source: George R.R. Martin, 'The Princess and the Queen' excerpt (primary text), Reactor/Tor.com
claims.quote: we must dance along with the rest
claims.page: Dangerous Women: The Princess and The Queen (Excerpt)

claims.claim: Before any scene, four abstract paragraphs summarize the war's claimants, scale, character and consequences; only then does the narrative descend to a dated day.
claims.source: George R.R. Martin, 'The Princess and the Queen' excerpt (primary text), Reactor/Tor.com
claims.page: Dangerous Women: The Princess and The Queen (Excerpt)

claims.claim: Sentences lean on triadic lists and 'and'-chains ('lords, knights, and smallfolk'; 'knives and lies and poison').
claims.source: George R.R. Martin, 'The Princess and the Queen' excerpt (primary text), Reactor/Tor.com
claims.page: Dangerous Women: The Princess and The Queen (Excerpt)

claims.claim: Archaic markers ('whilst', 'alarum', 'a moon's turn', 'the hour of the bat/owl') set the register without heavy Latinate vocabulary.
claims.source: George R.R. Martin, 'The Princess and the Queen' excerpt (primary text), Reactor/Tor.com
claims.page: Dangerous Women: The Princess and The Queen (Excerpt)

claims.claim: An asterisked footnote glosses how 'greens' and 'blacks' got their names at a tourney, importing scholarly apparatus into the narrative.
claims.source: George R.R. Martin, 'The Princess and the Queen' excerpt (primary text), Reactor/Tor.com
claims.page: Dangerous Women: The Princess and The Queen (Excerpt)

claims.claim: The chronicler attributes the war's poetic name to some singer, the chronicle's habit of assigning romance to song and sobriety to record.
claims.source: George R.R. Martin, 'The Princess and the Queen' excerpt (primary text), Reactor/Tor.com
claims.quote: No doubt the phrase originated with some singer.
claims.page: Dangerous Women: The Princess and The Queen (Excerpt)

claims.claim: A king's death is dated to the day and moon of a year and to a named hour, precision that reads as record rather than scene.
claims.source: George R.R. Martin, 'The Princess and the Queen' excerpt (primary text), Reactor/Tor.com
claims.page: Dangerous Women: The Princess and The Queen (Excerpt)
